name: Array
description: A fixed-size collection of elements stored in contiguous memory and accessed by index.

name: Linked List
description: A linear collection of nodes where each node points to the next, allowing efficient insertion and removal.

name: Stack
description: A LIFO (Last-In, First-Out) collection where elements are added and removed from the same end.

name: Queue
description: A FIFO (First-In, First-Out) collection where elements are added at the rear and removed from the front.

name: Hash Table
description: A structure that maps keys to values using a hash function for near-constant-time lookups.

name: Binary Search Tree
description: A hierarchical structure where each node has at most two children, keeping left subtree values smaller and right subtree values larger.

name: Graph
description: A set of nodes (vertices) connected by edges, used to model networks, relationships, and paths.

name: AVL Tree
description: A self-balancing BST that tracks balance factors and performs rotations after insertions to guarantee O(log n) height at all times.

name: Binary Heap
description: A complete binary tree stored as an array where every parent is ≤ its children (min-heap). Enables O(log n) insert and O(log n) extract-min.

name: Trie
description: A tree where each node represents one character. Paths from root to end-marked nodes spell stored words, enabling O(m) prefix search independent of dictionary size.

name: Skip List
description: A probabilistic multi-level linked list where higher levels act as express lanes, giving O(log n) expected search, insert, and delete without needing rotations.

name: Bubble Sort
description: Repeatedly swaps adjacent elements that are out of order until the list is sorted.

name: Selection Sort
description: Repeatedly selects the minimum element from the unsorted portion and moves it to the front.

name: Insertion Sort
description: Builds the sorted list one element at a time by inserting each value into its correct position among the already-sorted elements.

name: Merge Sort
description: A divide-and-conquer algorithm that splits the list in half, sorts each half, then merges them back together in order.

name: Quick Sort
description: A divide-and-conquer algorithm that partitions the list around a pivot, then recursively sorts the partitions in place.

name: Heap Sort
description: Builds a max-heap from the list, then repeatedly extracts the largest element to the end to produce a sorted array in place.

name: Counting Sort
description: Counts occurrences of each value and uses prefix sums to place every element directly into its final position — no comparisons needed.

name: Radix Sort
description: Sorts integers digit by digit from least to most significant, using a stable counting sort at each position to achieve linear time on fixed-width keys.

name: Breadth-First Search
description: Explores a graph level by level using a queue, visiting all neighbors before moving deeper. Finds the shortest path in unweighted graphs.

name: Depth-First Search
description: Explores as far as possible along each branch before backtracking, using a stack or recursion. Basis for cycle detection, topological sort and connected components.

name: Dijkstra's Algorithm
description: Finds the least-cost path from a source on a weighted graph with non-negative edges by greedily settling the closest unvisited node using a priority queue.

name: A* Search
description: An informed shortest-path search that guides Dijkstra toward the goal using an admissible heuristic (f = g + h), exploring far fewer nodes while staying optimal.

name: Neural Network (Backpropagation)
description: A multi-layer perceptron trained by backpropagation with gradient descent. Learns to tell CONFIRMED exoplanets from FALSE POSITIVEs using only the physical features of each Kepler candidate — a supervised learning example on real NASA data.

name: K-Means Clustering
description: An unsupervised algorithm that groups points into k clusters by alternating assignment and centroid updates (Lloyd's algorithm). Discovers structure in the exoplanet catalog with no labels — an unsupervised learning counterpart to the network above.
